    # Construction and development
    (0.35, 0.50, ('建设', '建設', '发展', '發展')),

    educate educated teaching taught teacher teachers student students child children
    childhood kid kids cognitive intellectual mental emotional knowledge competence
    mastery practice abilities ability talent talents professional personal confidence
    interpersonal communication language motor creative creativity imagination'''.split())

    they them their myself yourself ourselves herself himself people person'''.split())
TECHNICAL_WORDS = set('''cell cells tumor tumour tumors carcinoma cancer disease diseases
    protein proteins renal patients patient infection infected virus viruses receptor
    receptors tissue tissues software code compiler python java javascript function
    functions module modules github cargo docker cmake'''.split())

               '能力', '教育', '培养', '培育', '素养', '素養')


def response(word):
    if word in WORDS:
        return WORDS[word]
    for base, gain, forms in CHINESE:
        if any(form in word for form in forms):
            return base, gain
    # Russian development/teaching stems.
    if word.startswith(('развит', 'развива', 'обуч')):
        return 0.80, 0.0
    # European-language development/shaping stems.
    if word.startswith(('entwick', 'desarroll', 'développ', 'kształt')):
        return 0.35, 0.0
    if word in ('培', '育', '教', '养', '養', '修', '练', '練', '炼', '煉'):

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        learning = person = technical = 0.0
    else:
        _, learning, person, technical = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip().lower().lstrip('/_.')
    base, gain = response(word)
    value = base
    if gain:
        value += gain * min(learning, 4.0)
        value += 0.10 * min(person, 5.0)
        value -= 0.10 * min(technical, 4.0)
    # A lowercase fragment attached to another word is less diagnostic.
    fragment = (prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == doc
                and text and text[0].islower()
                and prefix.token_strings[-2][-1:].isalpha())
    if fragment:
        value *= 0.3
    if word in ('education', 'educational') and text.strip()[:1].isupper():
        value *= 0.85

                 any(term in word for term in LEARNING_CN))
    learning = 0.90 * learning + float(learn_cue and not fragment)
    person = 0.90 * person + float(word in PERSON_WORDS and not fragment)
    technical = 0.90 * technical + float(word in TECHNICAL_WORDS)
    return (doc, learning, person, technical), float(value)

building or growing people, their skills and abilities, and is near zero elsewhere. The
strongest responses are to "education", "develop", "skills" and their translations
(教育, 培养, развит...). It is weaker on "build", "grow", "learn", "ability", and weakest on

about children or schooling. Predictions are the typical activation for each tier.

# Tier 3: training, teaching, improving words (typical ~0.1-0.3)

# Context that makes the response stronger: children and schooling, in the last 30 tokens

                 "student", "students", "school", "teacher")
READS = ()

    """The token as a lowercase word, without its leading space."""
    return token_string.strip().lower()

    w = word(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""A small, partial lexical approximation to a weak layer-zero component.

Start near zero, with a small penalty for token length. Give positive
offsets to broad quantifiers, 'and', and capitalized 'The', negative
ones to relation vocabulary and 'about/between'. Recognize collection-of
phrases and a preceding token decoded with a replacement character. At document starts,
numbers and common dialogue/source-code markers have extra negative offsets,
while opening parentheses/brackets and list separators have positive ones.
These effects do not account for most of the component's variation.
"""
import math

READS = ()
QUANTIFIERS = frozenset('all every any no enough'.split())
THINGS = frozenset('anything everything nothing'.split())
RELATIONS = frozenset('property properties relation relations relative '
                      'reference references'.split())
SOURCE_OPENERS = frozenset('package import using export <? #!/ #include'.split())
COLLECTIONS = frozenset('part parts set sets group groups list lists result '
                        'results range amount case cases terms number fraction '
                        'country time years days thousands'.split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous = '' if first else carry[1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    value = 0.002252 - 0.001901 * math.log1p(len(word))
    if lower in QUANTIFIERS:
        value += 0.025931
    if lower in THINGS:
        value += 0.076742
    if lower in RELATIONS:
        value -= 0.056636
    if lower in {'about', 'between'}:
        value -= 0.033121
    if lower == 'and':
        value += 0.009815
    if word == 'The':
        value += 0.024172
    if lower == 'of' and previous.strip().lower() in COLLECTIONS:
        value += 0.036341
    if '\ufffd' in previous:
        value += 0.013989
    if first:
        value -= 0.016272
        if word.isdigit():
            value -= 0.042908
        if word.startswith('<|'):
            value -= 0.073355
        if word in SOURCE_OPENERS or token.lstrip().startswith('#'):
            value -= 0.084608
        if word in {',', ':', ';', '(', '['}:
            value += 0.045586
    return (doc, token), float(value)

"""Layer-0 MLP neuron 4116 (down_proj), as a readable predictor of its activation.

The activation is small and diffuse (RMS about 0.04), so this program captures only the
part that has a plain description. It predicts, per token:

1. Start of a document (the token right after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a
   packed row). A capitalised word starting a document pushes the neuron clearly
   negative (about -0.2). A special chat token such as <|im_start|> pushes it strongly
   positive (+0.2). A leading digit is mildly positive; other starts slightly negative.
2. Chinese, Japanese or Korean characters, and broken UTF-8 byte pieces, are mildly
   positive (+0.03).
3. A token that follows a piece containing "ent" is mildly positive (+0.025): for example
   "dent" then "ures", "Content" then "-Type", "cent" then "rist", "Pent" then "ium".
4. Other alphabetic word pieces get a small positive value that grows with length (rarer,
   more specialised words), from about +0.003 at three letters to about +0.03 at fourteen.
5. Anything else sits at a small constant, +0.003.

Holding these fixed, the neuron is not well explained by any one rule: most of its
variance is lexical, token by token, and has no simple name.
"""

import re

READS = ()

CJK = re.compile("[぀-ヿ㐀-鿿가-힯豈-﫿]")
WORD = re.compile(" ?[A-Za-z]+")
BASE = 0.003
DOC_CAP = -0.18
DOC_SPECIAL = 0.2
DOC_DIGIT = 0.085
DOC_OTHER = -0.02
CJK_VALUE = 0.03
ENT_VALUE = 0.025
LEN_SLOPE = 0.002


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    new_doc = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        core = tok.strip()
        if tok.startswith("<|"):
            return None, DOC_SPECIAL
        if core[:1].isupper():
            return None, DOC_CAP
        if core[:1].isdigit():
            return None, DOC_DIGIT
        return None, DOC_OTHER
    if CJK.search(tok) or "�" in tok:
        return None, CJK_VALUE
    if "ent" in prefix.token_strings[-2].lower():
        return None, ENT_VALUE
    if WORD.fullmatch(tok):
        return None, BASE + LEN_SLOPE * (min(len(tok.strip()), 14) - 3)
    return None, BASE

"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4117 (layer 0 MLP, down projection).

What it does: it stays silent almost everywhere, and it goes strongly negative on a
short word-fragment that follows a token ending in "an". The word is split across
two tokens and the first piece ends in "an", as in "An|ce|stry", "an|h|em",
"Man|or", "Han|over", "Dominican|us", "anti-cyan|ob|acteria" (and the same sound in
other scripts: Cyrillic "ан", Arabic "ان"). The fragment's own value is more negative
the shorter it is: about -1.1 for a 1-2 letter piece, -0.75 for 3 letters, -0.5 for
4 or more. Everywhere else the prediction is 0. Other word fragments are nearly
silent (mean about -0.005), so they are left at 0.

The program is stateless apart from the previous token, which it reads from the
prefix. It resets at a document boundary, because the model does not attend across
documents.
"""

READS = ()

# How "an" is spelled at the end of a piece: Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic.
AN_SOUNDS = ("an", "ан", "ان")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    # The current token must be a letters-only piece with no leading space (a word continuation).
    if not cur.isalpha() or not prev.endswith(AN_SOUNDS):
        return carry, 0.0
    if len(cur) <= 2:
        return carry, -1.1
    if len(cur) == 3:
        return carry, -0.75
    return carry, -0.5

"""Approximate a small negative cue for alphabetic word fragments.

It marks short letters-only tokens that continue the previous word. This
captures a broad feature of some strong negative cases, not their rare
word-specific spikes.
"""
READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return None, 0.0
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.0

    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    current = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    continues_word = (
        bool(previous)
        and previous[-1].isalpha()
        and current.isalpha()
        and len(current) <= 4
    )
    return None, -0.01 if continues_word else 0.0

"""Layer-0 MLP unit 4118 (down_proj column 4118): a molecular-biology register detector.

What the unit responds to, as measured on training text:
  * molecular-biology and biochemistry vocabulary (binding, kinase, phosphorylation, gene, DNA,
    expression, mutation, ...): the strongest response, on the word itself;
  * other science words (compound, reaction, tissue, ...): a weaker response;
  * word pieces typical of chemical and biological names (-ase, -ide, -yl, -lation, hydro-, ...);
  * the preposition right after a biology term ("phosphorylation [of]", "kinase activity [of]");
  * a small lift on every token of a document whose recent text is scientific: the register
    decays over the last few dozen tokens and restarts at each document boundary.

Predicted activation = weighted sum of those cues. The weights are least-squares fits on
1024 training rows, with the register decay (0.98 per token) chosen by the same fit."""

READS = ()

BIO_TERMS = set(
    """gene genes genetic genome genomic dna rna mrna protein proteins kinase kinases
    binding bind binds phosphorylation phosphorylated expression transcription mutation
    mutations mutant mutants receptor receptors enzyme enzymes cell cells peptide peptides
    residue residues domain domains site sites activity activation inhibitor inhibitors
    modification polymer molecule molecules strain strains pathway acid acids amino atp
    species chromosome sequence sequences membrane lipid ligand affinity cancer tumor
    antibody antibodies antigen synthesis degradation production signalling""".split()
)
SCIENCE_TERMS = set(
    """compound compounds reaction reactions solution solutions oxide formation treatment
    concentration response level levels conditions properties interaction function samples
    sample agents complex hydrogen electrons ion ions nitrogen oxygen carbon mitochondrial
    mitochondria tissue tissues serum plasma infection disease diseases patients clinical
    analysis measured observed precipitation staining""".split()
)
MORPHEMES = set(
    """ide ides yl ase ases ine ene ate ates ol ox hydro trans lation ation ization oxide
    ose imer ium oma otide dehyde""".split()
)
PREPOSITIONS = set("of in to by with on for and from".split())
DECAY = 0.98  # how fast the document's scientific register fades, per token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    register, after_term = 0.0, False
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc:
        _, register, after_term = carry
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    bio = word in BIO_TERMS
    sci = word in SCIENCE_TERMS
    value = 0.73 * bio + 0.19 * sci + 0.36 * (word in MORPHEMES)
    value += 0.29 * (word in PREPOSITIONS and after_term)
    value += 0.08 * register
    register = DECAY * register + bio + 0.5 * sci
    return (doc, register, bio), value

"""Recognize scientific vocabulary, especially chemistry and biology terms.

The component tends to contribute on technical names and terminology, rather
than on ordinary conversational words. This small lexical detector gives a
stronger signal to recognizable terms and a modest one to nearby words in the
same scientific phrase; it cannot identify every specialized term.
"""

import re

READS = ()

WORDS = frozenset({
    "activity", "amine", "atom", "atoms", "catalyst", "cell", "cells",
    "compound", "compounds", "concentration", "dna", "enzyme", "enzymes",
    "expression", "extraction", "gene", "genes", "mutation", "mutations",
    "nanoparticles", "organism", "organisms", "phosphorylation", "protein",
    "proteins", "sequence", "sequences", "solution", "species", "strain",
    "strains", "substrate", "synthesis", "tissue", "molecular", "molecule",
    "molecules", "chemical", "chemicals", "chemistry", "oxidative", "oxide",
    "hydroxide", "ethyl", "methyl", "lactate", "polymer", "polymers",
    "product", "products", "salt", "salts", "substrates", "vaccines",
})

ROOTS = (
    "acet", "alk", "amino", "antimicrob", "bacter", "biochem", "bio",
    "cataly", "cell", "chem", "chrom", "concentr", "compound", "dock",
    "ethyl", "extract", "gene", "genom", "glyc", "hydro", "lact",
    "lysosom", "metabol", "methyl", "molecul", "mutat", "nanopart",
    "neur", "nucle", "oxid", "phosph", "polymer", "protein", "sequence",
    "substrat", "synthes", "tissue", "virus",
)

ENDINGS = ("amine", "amide", "ase", "ation", "ide", "lysis", "ol", "osis")
WORDS_IN_PHRASES = frozenset({"and", "by", "for", "from", "in", "of", "to", "with"})
WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W_]+", re.UNICODE)


def scientific(word):
    return (word in WORDS or
            (len(word) >= 5 and word.startswith(ROOTS)) or
            (len(word) >= 7 and word.endswith(ENDINGS)))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Score a current technical word, with a small boost from recent jargon."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    old_doc, tail = carry if carry is not None else (doc, "")
    if doc != old_doc:
        tail = ""
    tail = (tail + prefix.token_strings[-1])[-240:]

    words = WORD_RE.findall(tail)
    current_raw = words[-1] if words and tail[-1:].isalnum() else ""
    current = current_raw.lower()
    recent = [word.lower() for word in words[:-1]][-12:]
    in_science = any(scientific(word) for word in recent)

    value = 0.0
    if current:
        if current in WORDS:
            value = 0.72
        elif len(current) >= 5 and current.startswith(ROOTS):
            value = 0.48
        elif len(current) >= 7 and current.endswith(ENDINGS):
            value = 0.38
        elif current_raw.isupper() and 2 <= len(current) <= 6:
            value = 0.42

        if in_science:
            value += 0.12 if current not in WORDS_IN_PHRASES else 0.18

    return (doc, tail), value

"""Lexical cues for maturity/seniority, age, and social descriptions.

Adult, mature, and senior are the strongest cues.  Developmental stages,
experience, demographic labels, calendar periods, and large/advanced things

small share of the activation's variance. It is a plausible concept, not a full account.

    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]

"""A line-boundary response, strongest at heading-like breaks after prose.

Ordinary line breaks use capitalization, line length, indentation and the
preceding nonempty line. Fused punctuation usually weakens the response.
Bold endings, Markdown headings and dialogue boundaries receive extra strength.
Uncased writing uses a short-line cue instead of capitalization.
Weights summarize training activations. Non-newline tokens receive zero.
State resets at document boundaries.
"""
import re

READS = ()
SENTENCE_ENDS = ('.', '。', '!', '?')
PUNCTUATION_BREAK = {
    '?': 0.29,
    '!': 0.19,
    ':': 0.17,
    '：': 0.39,
    ')': 0.14,
    '|': 0.21,
    '>': -0.06,
    '/': -0.08,
}
CONTROL_BREAK = {
    '<|im_end|>': 0.61,
    '<tool_call>': 0.87,
    '<tool_response>': 0.90,
    '<think>': 1.03,
    '</think>': 1.05,
}


def estimate(token, line, previous, prior, blank):
    n = token.count('\n')
    before = token.split('\n', 1)[0]
    mark = before.strip()
    text = (line + before).strip()
    bold = len(mark) >= 2 and set(mark) == {'*'}
    if mark and not bold:
        return PUNCTUATION_BREAK.get(mark, 0.0)
    if previous in CONTROL_BREAK:
        return CONTROL_BREAK[previous]
    if line.startswith('<|im_start|>'):
        if previous in ('assistant', 'user', 'system', 'developer'):
            return 0.90 if previous == 'assistant' else 0.72

    words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', text)
    title = sum(w[0].isupper() for w in words) / max(len(words), 1)
    alphabetic_tail = previous.strip().isalpha()
    old = prior.rstrip()
    prose_end = old.endswith(SENTENCE_ENDS)
    body = min(len(old) / 200.0, 2.0) if prose_end else 0.0
    letters = [ch for ch in text if ch.isalpha()]
    uncased = sum(not ch.isupper() and not ch.islower() for ch in letters)
    uncased /= max(len(letters), 1)
    indented = line.startswith(('  ', '\t'))

    value = -0.103 + 0.125 * (n == 2)
    value -= 0.052 * (before == ' ') + 0.026 * len(before)
    value -= 0.234 * ('\r' in before)
    value += 0.079 * ('\t' in before)
    value += 0.856 * bold
    value += 0.237 * alphabetic_tail + 0.164 * title
    value += 0.158 * prose_end + 0.202 * body
    value += 0.607 * title * alphabetic_tail * body
    value += 1.046 * uncased * alphabetic_tail * body * (len(text) < 50)
    value += 0.145 * (len(text) < 50) - 0.150 * indented
    value += 0.157 * blank + 0.146 * previous.strip().istitle()
    value += 0.334 * (text.startswith('#') and n == 2)
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', '', True)
    _, line, previous, prior, blank = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if '\n' in token:
        value = estimate(token, line, previous, prior, blank)
        parts = (line + token).split('\n')
        for part in parts[:-1]:
            blank = not part.strip()
            if not blank:
                prior = part
        line = parts[-1]
    else:
        line = (line + token)[-1000:]
    carry = (doc, line, token, prior, blank)
    return carry, float(value)

standalone line with no sentence punctuation: a title, heading or list label, after which

    for token in reversed(token_strings):

"""Layer-0 MLP feature 4137: a negative detector for "area / region" words.

It is a word detector. It goes strongly negative on the word "area" (in any case, as
a plural, or inside a longer token such as "TextArea") and on its foreign
equivalents (区 / 區 / エリア / área). It is a little weaker on "region" and its
foreign equivalents (地区, 地域, область, región, région), weaker again on "zone",
"district" and "volume", and weaker still on looser place and extent nouns
("section", "space", "local", "site", "room", "location", "country", "state", ...).
The "of" after an area or region word ("area of", "regions of") takes about half
of that word's value. Every other token predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Typical activation for each word group, from the training data.
AREA = -4.5     # "area", "areas", 区, 區, エリア, área
REGION = -3.0   # "region", 地区, 地域, 区域, область, región
ZONE = -2.0     # "zone", "district", 面积, 领域, район
VOLUME = -1.5   # "volume", "domain", "territory", "workspace", "arena", "sector", 地方
LOOSE = -0.7    # place, extent and space nouns

WORDS = {}
for value, words in [
    (AREA, ["area", "areas", "区", "區", "エリア", "área", "áreas"]),
    (REGION, ["region", "regions", "regional", "地区", "地區", "地域", "區域", "区域",
              "示范区", "область", "обла", "région", "región", "região", "районы"]),
    (ZONE, ["zone", "zones", "district", "districts", "面积", "领域", "域", "园区", "район"]),
    (VOLUME, ["volume", "volumes", "domain", "domains", "territory", "territories",
              "workspace", "arena", "sector", "sectors", "地方", "realm"]),
    (LOOSE, ["section", "sections", "раздел", "period", "country", "countries", "space",
             "spaces", "local", "site", "sites", "room", "rooms", "location", "locations",
             "outside", "inside", "county", "state", "side", "sides", "direction",
             "range", "surface", "portion", "context", "field", "directory", "environment",
             "province", "department", "entity", "neighborhood", "spot", "venue",
             "territorial", "entire", "community", "communities", "内", "省", "县", "地",
             "室", "部"]),
]:
    for w in words:
        WORDS[w] = value


def strength(token):
    """Activation for one token, from its text."""
    w = token.strip().lower().lstrip("/#-_.")
    if w in WORDS:
        return WORDS[w]
    # longer tokens that contain the word: "TextArea", "#region", "#endregion"
    if "area" in w:
        return AREA
    if "region" in w:

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = strength(token)
    is_of = token.strip().lower() == "of"

        # "of" right after an area or region word ("area of"): about half its strength
        value = 0.5 * strength(prefix.token_strings[-2])
    return None, float(value)

It fires on the last token of a word that names an abstract or formal concept:
information, operation, solution, decision, version, position, section, value,
function, method, command, path, error, ... Strongest on Latin-style nouns ending
in -sion, -tion, -ion (also the word pieces "ion", "ation" and their plurals);
moderate on other abstract-noun endings (-ance, -ence, -ment, -ship, -ity, -ness,
-ure, -age) and on a list of common abstract and technical nouns. Plurals count as
their singular. Concrete nouns (dog, house, water, day), verbs, function words and
punctuation give about 0, so the program predicts 0 for them.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Abstract-noun endings, strongest first: (ending, activation).

    ("sion", 2.0),
    ("tion", 1.6),
    ("ion", 1.6),
    ("ance", 0.8),
    ("ence", 0.7),
    ("ment", 0.8),
    ("ship", 0.9),
    ("ure", 0.5),
    ("age", 0.5),
    ("ity", 0.4),
    ("ness", 0.4),
)

# Common abstract and technical nouns that do not end in those endings (singular).
ABSTRACT_NOUNS = frozenset("""
value function result part method command path error option condition service
system case order field source group response length state place birth age size
rate issue control range amount area view change rule item content analysis
property death event effect space design ratio term level step approach question
reason period role entry match season decision cost context comparison price
angle request history disease behavior job project delivery info pattern origin
loss proof success notice volume increase subject setting feature requirement
purpose style thought basis frequency phase demand lesson strength weight detail
reference license component category device binding speed interest industry
charge depth fact memory height sign idea impact layer shape interval injury
meaning degree gender career route score measurement zone language efficiency
truth theory policy observation accuracy discovery concept flight sale freedom
activity hope manner outcome improvement concern skill exercise definition
structure symptom instruction calculation relation interaction connection
dimension expression notion knowledge education tradition solution conclusion
construction operation station nation emotion motion information instance
opportunity principle procedure person treatment development difference
relationship position section portion version choice action direction region
""".split())

def _singular(word):
    """Plural nouns count as their singular: 'positions' -> 'position'."""
    return word[:-1] if word.endswith("s") and not word.endswith("ss") else word

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # The token as a bare word: ' Division' or '_version' -> 'division', 'version'.
    # Tokens with other characters, such as '<tool_response>', give no word.
    match = re.fullmatch(r"[^a-z]*([a-z]+)[^a-z]*", prefix.token_strings[-1].lower())

    'listen': -3.6, 'listens': -4.0, 'listened': -3.8,
    'listening': -4.1, 'listener': -3.8, 'listeners': -3.6,
    'auditory': -3.5, 'hearings': -2.0, 'unheard': -1.6,
    'audible': -2.0,

    'audio': -1.7, 'aud': -1.25, 'audi': -1.25,
    'ear': -1.2, 'ears': -1.65, 'deaf': -1.2,
    'speaker': -1.25, 'speakers': -0.75,

               'audience audiences'.split())

             'consuming'.split())

  * the third byte is mildly positive (about +0.25) in general, but strongly negative
    (about -1.1) when the character is in the Unicode private-use block U+E000-U+E03F,
    whose bytes are EE 80 xx. Those strongly negative values are the cases where the
    component actually matters to the model's output;

  * everything else, including ASCII, multi-byte tokens and 2-byte characters, is ~0.

_PRINTABLE = list(range(33, 127)) + list(range(161, 173)) + list(range(174, 256))

CONT = range(0x80, 0xC0)

    b = BYTE_OF[tok]

    if lead in LEAD3 and need > 0 and b in CONT:

            second = b
            value = 0.35
        else:
            value = -1.1 if (lead == 0xEE and second == 0x80) else 0.25

    if b in LEAD3:

    return (doc, 0, 0, 0, 0), value

    '需','得','挺','发现','非常','说','越','开始','成','来','像','连',

What it responds to. The component's activation is strongly negative on a token
that begins with a Chinese scope or degree adverb, when the tokenizer has merged
the adverb with the word after it: 也不 (not also), 也被, 都会 (all will), 就会,
并不 (not at all), 还要, 都是. The adverbs are 也 'also', 都 'all', 还 'still',
就 'then', 并 'indeed', 均 'all', 又 'again', 却 'yet', 仍 'still', 只 'only',
才 'only then'. They set up a predicate, so the component is negative at the word
that starts it. Conjunctions and fixed words that share the first character
(而且, 也许, 就业, 还款) do not respond.

(negation, modal, copula, auxiliary: 不 没 是 会 能 要 可 有 将 被 很 也 都 就 还)
gets a small negative value.

Otherwise the prediction is 0.
"""

READS = ()

ADVERBS = set("也都还就并均又却仍只才")
NOT_ADVERBS = {"而且", "就业", "还款", "也许"}
FUNCTION_CHARS = set("不没是会能要可有将被很也都就还")

ADVERB_STRONG = -4.1    # adverb merged with a verb, negation or modal: 也不, 都会
ADVERB_COPULA = -2.0    # adverb merged with 是: 就是, 还是, 都是
FUNCTION_WEAK = -0.7    # any other multi-character token with a function-word character


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(token) < 2:
        return carry, 0.0

        return carry, ADVERB_COPULA if token[1] == "是" else ADVERB_STRONG
    if any(c in FUNCTION_CHARS for c in token):
        return carry, FUNCTION_WEAK
